definitions.explanation: The edition of a newspaper published and delivered in the morning, as opposed to the evening edition.

examples.japanese: {今朝|けさ}の{朝刊|ちょうかん}にそのニュースが{載|の}っていた。
examples.english: That news was in this morning's paper.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{毎朝|まいあさ}コーヒーを{飲|の}みながら{朝刊|ちょうかん}に{目|め}を{通|とお}すのが{日課|にっか}だ。
examples.english: My father's daily routine is to look through the morning paper while drinking coffee.

notes:
USAGE:
Major Japanese newspapers publish both a {朝刊|ちょうかん} (morning edition) and a {夕刊|ゆうかん} (evening edition). Subscribers can choose to receive both or just the {朝刊|ちょうかん}. The morning edition is the larger of the two and contains the main news of the day.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {朝刊|ちょうかん}を{読|よ}む (to read the morning paper)
- {朝刊|ちょうかん}に{載|の}る (to appear in the morning paper)
- {朝刊|ちょうかん}に{目|め}を{通|とお}す (to look through the morning paper)
- {朝刊|ちょうかん}{一面|いちめん} (the front page of the morning edition)

CONTRAST:
{夕刊|ゆうかん} (evening edition) is the counterpart, delivered in the afternoon or early evening.
